title: Reference approach: Compiler Experiment
answer: Implement compiler experiment in a small isolated script. Required implementation evidence includes: torch.compile, time.perf_counter. Use a reproducible seed, report observed output, and explain relevant edge cases.
explanation: This exercise consolidates the topic from lesson 128. The list of required strings is only a minimal static signal; inspect numerical correctness, error handling, and test outcomes manually.
example_code:
import time, torch
model=torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(16,64),torch.nn.ReLU(),torch.nn.Linear(64,4)).eval(); x=torch.randn(32,16)
start=time.perf_counter(); eager=model(x); eager_s=time.perf_counter()-start
compiled=torch.compile(model); compiled(x) # compile/warm-up overhead is separate
print(eager.shape, round(eager_s,6)) # Compare steady state after repeated warm-up on target hardware.
